front: What two signals does this page's video RAG pipeline index, and how are they linked?
back: A Whisper speech-to-text transcript and frames sampled at a fixed interval, linked only by arithmetic on a shared timestamp axis -- not a shared index or joint embedding space.

front: Are frames embedded against the query in this pipeline?
back: No. Only the transcript is searched by cosine similarity; the matching frame is found afterward by nearest timestamp to whichever transcript segment search retrieved.

front: What are the three tiers of 'video RAG,' and which one does this page build?
back: Tier 1: decomposed transcript+frame retrieval (this page). Tier 2: native omni models taking real video+audio input (Gemini, Qwen2.5-Omni). Tier 3: video-native embedding of whole clips (InternVideo/ViCLIP).

front: Why does this page use tier 1 instead of tier 2 (native video input)?
back: The generation model used here (Claude) has no video content-block type in its API -- only image and document -- so it structurally cannot take a video file as input.

front: What was the measured transcript-only Recall@3, and what caused the two failures?
back: 3 of 5. One failure: Whisper split a cause from its explanation across two adjacent segments (a chunk-boundary problem on the time axis). The other: near-duplicate segments about similar percentages crowded the correct one out of the top-3.

front: How is a retrieved frame chosen once a transcript segment wins search?
back: The frame at the fixed 5-second sample point numerically closest to the segment's start timestamp -- simple nearest-neighbor on time, never guaranteed to be the exact right visual instant.

front: What question can transcript-only retrieval never answer, and why?
back: What the whiteboard's Y-axis label says -- it's shown on screen but never spoken, so no amount of better text retrieval recovers it; only passing the actual frame image answers it.

front: What does this recipe deliberately leave out of its pipeline?
back: A separate CLIP-based visual frame search -- frame grounding here is purely timestamp-proximity to the retrieved transcript segment, not a query embedded against frame images directly.
